text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000028 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation, mostly on low-complexity patients, but no 99215 charts were returned to test whether the documentation supports it.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern points toward upcoding. The 99215 share runs above the all-provider rate in every complexity band, and most of this provider's 99215 claims fall on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. Sampled examples such as C0013601, C0013964 and C0014978 (Z09 follow-up only) and C0013984 and C0015156 (R21 rash) are hard to square with high-complexity MDM. The sampled high-complexity 99215 claims (e.g., C0014117, C0014493) look clinically plausible, so not every top-level visit is in question. The documentation cannot settle this yet: only 16 charts came back, none of them 99215, and the 99213/99214 notes that did return all supported the billed level with no signs of inflated data review. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with the Z09, R21 and M54.50 visits, and check whether the documented MDM and time support level 5."}
